scenes.label: Opening Hook
scenes.audio: When a customer tells you it's too expensive, what's your first reaction?

scenes.label: Product Information
scenes.audio: Calculate a discount for him? Then you're finished. 'Too expensive' has four meanings. Are you clear on which one it is?

scenes.label: Product Selling Points
scenes.audio: First, he really doesn't have the budget. So what you need to do is not offer a discount, but to help him do the math.

scenes.label: Usage Scenarios
scenes.audio: 36,000 a year sounds like a lot, but 100 a day seems okay, right?

scenes.label: Product Selling Points
scenes.audio: Second, he feels it's not worth it. It is definitely not a price issue, it's a trust issue.

scenes.label: Problem Solving
scenes.audio: He doesn't trust you. Whatever you say, he discounts it.

scenes.label: Product Selling Points
scenes.audio: At this time, what you need to supplement is not a discount, but trust.

scenes.label: Product Selling Points
scenes.audio: Third, he is testing you. Experienced people are used to haggling. The more easily you lower the price, the more he feels your price is not genuine. If you hold your price, he respects you instead.

scenes.label: Usage Scenarios
scenes.audio: Fourth, he doesn't even want to buy. 'Too expensive' is just his most convenient reason for rejection.

scenes.label: Call to Action
scenes.audio: So what you should do is go back and pull his motivation, not deal with the price. Four situations have four solutions, but the underlying logic is only one. Customers don't believe because the product is good, but they start listening to how good the product is because they believe in you first. I'm Tai Xin, I'll take you through human nature to close high-value deals. Comment 'Too expensive' and I'll send you the full SOP.
